content: 1. Bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide are administered as a single tablet taken orally once daily. 2. Bictegravir increases the plasma levels or effects of dofetilide by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is contraindicated. Bictegravir inhibits organic cation transporter 2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter 1 (MATE1) in vitro. Co-administration with OCT2 and MATE1 substrates may elevate their plasma concentrations. 3. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels or effects of bictegravir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers can significantly reduce bictegravir plasma concentrations, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance development. 4. Antiretroviral (ART) medications may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous cell therapies such as atidarsagene autotemcel and betibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization or until the expected duration for medication elimination. ARTs should also be avoided until all apheresis cycles are completed. 5. Carbamazepine reduces bictegravir plasma levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance. Alternative anticonvulsants should be considered. 6. Elivaldogene autotemcel and bictegravir may interfere with each other. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 7. Enasidenib increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP transporters. Co-administration with sensitive substrates of these transporters should be avoided. If unavoidable, substrate dosages should be reduced as per prescribing information. 8. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to tenofovir alafenamide. Co-administration should be avoided or monitored closely. 9. Tenofovir alafenamide reduces the levels or effects of letermovir by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Co-administration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 10. Bictegravir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel interactions require ART discontinuation at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require longer discontinuation periods. 11. Oxcarbazepine decreases bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. Alternative anticonvulsants should be considered. 12. Phenobarbital reduces bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. Alternative anticonvulsants should be considered. 13. Phenytoin decreases bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. Alternative anticonvulsants should be considered. 14. Rifabutin reduces bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. 15. Rifapentine decreases bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. 16. St. John’s Wort reduces bictegravir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A and UGT1A1 inducers is not recommended. 17. Sotorasib decreases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inducing P-gp efflux transporter. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 18. Acalabrutinib increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Aluminum hydroxide reduces bictegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions two hours before or six hours after antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Simultaneous administration is not recommended. 20. Calcium carbonate reduces bictegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken with food alongside calcium-containing supplements but not under fasting conditions. 21. Ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate reduce bictegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken with food alongside iron-containing supplements but not under fasting conditions. 22. Fostamatinib increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting BCRP metabolism. Monitor for toxicities and consider dosage reductions of BCRP substrate drugs. 23. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting BCRP metabolism. Monitor plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. 24. Ifosfamide and tenofovir alafenamide co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Monitor renal function and electrolytes closely. 25. Istradefylline increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 26. Lonafarnib increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by weakly inhibiting P-gp. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. 27. Magnesium citrate, magnesium gluconate, magnesium hydroxide, and magnesium oxide reduce bictegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions two hours before or six hours after antacids containing magnesium. Simultaneous administration is not recommended. 28. Magnesium supplements may chelate with bictegravir, reducing its absorption. Administer bictegravir under fasting conditions two hours before or six hours after polyvalent cation administration. 29. Danicopan increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter. Monitor plasma concentrations and consider dose reductions of P-gp substrates. 30. Darolutamide increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid co-administration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reductions of BCRP substrate drugs. 31. Duvelisib levels or effects are reduced by tenofovir alafenamide via P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Elagolix increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Encorafenib increases tenofovir alafenamide levels or effects by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and adjust substrate doses as needed. 34. Ferric maltol reduces bictegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken with food alongside iron-containing supplements but not under fasting conditions.
